title: Logchain gap walkthrough notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal walk-through and breadcrumb trail for the "log chain" gaps we've been seeing since 2025-10-15. Not a polished incident postmortem — a working set of observations, commands I ran, and hypotheses to hand to whoever picks this up next.

High-level symptom:
- Sporadic span/trace gaps spanning ~30s-3m windows where frontend request shows up in HTTP logs, but no corresponding spans make it into Jaeger/Trace store and some metrics drop (span-per-request metric down ~40% for 2–5 minute bursts).
- Correlated with elevated kafka consumer lag on obs-ingest-01 for partition set A.

Why I care (quick):
- Affects user-facing debugging and alert fidelity (incidents look broader than they are).
- Can cause rollout regressions: A/B test traffic missing traces -> wrong rollback decisions.

Timeline (short):
- 2025-10-15 09:23 UTC: First spike noticed by Grafana alert (trace-coverage-drop).
- 2025-10-15 09:25–09:28 UTC: spike in obs-ingest consumer lag.
- 2025-10-16 13:10 UTC: repeat; opened OBS-412.
- 2025-11-03 16:40 UTC: manual debugging session; recorded commands below.

Commands I ran (raw, in order):
1) Check kafka consumer lag (kowl/cli):
   kubectl -n observability exec -it deploy/kafka-tools -- bash -c "kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.svc:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest"
   -> saw lag jump to ~120k for partitions 3,4,7 during spike window.

2) Inspect obs-ingest pod logs around 2025-10-15T09:25:00Z:
   kubectl -n observability logs deploy/obs-ingest-01 --since=10m | grep -i "drop\|error\|span" -n
   -> repeated warnings: "ingester: unknown trace parent, skipping span" and intermittent ERROR: "otlp: failed to unmarshal resource labels: unknown key service.version=1.2.+"

3) Pull a sample HTTP log and search for traceparent headers:
   jq '.[] | select(.path=="/api/complete") | {ts:.timestamp,traceparent:.headers.traceparent}' http-logs-2025-10-15.json | head -n 20
   -> ~60% of requests had traceparent header; missing ones aligned to gaps (not perfect).

4) Check otel-collector -> obs-ingest connection metrics:
   kubectl -n observability exec -it deploy/otel-collector -- curl localhost:8888/metrics | grep -E "otlp_received_spans|otlp_dropped_spans"
   -> otlp_received_spans drops coincide with gaps; otlp_dropped_spans non-zero but small (usually <10).

5) Reproduce locally by replaying a small batch through kafka-producer script (using headers preserved):
   python tools/replayer.py --topic telemetry.v1 --file sample-requests.json --preserve-headers
   -> Replayer produced spans; obs-ingest accepted them when traceparent present. When replayer stripped traceparent header, obs-ingest still accepted spans but they showed up as orphaned traces (no root).

Observed error snippets (copied):
- "ingester: unknown trace parent, skipping span id=0x7f3a..."
- "WARN pipeline/queue.go: slow consumer detected: pull duration 1820ms"
- "otlp: failed to unmarshal resource labels: unknown key service.version=1.2.+"
- "kafka: message.timestamp out of order, offset gap detected"

Quick interpretation notes (my head):
- There's a mix of problems: some spans legitimately lost (consumer lag, slow consumption), some spans malformed due to unexpected resource labels from a newer SDK rollout, some entries lacking traceparent header (frontend instrumentation sometimes drops header on 3xx/redirects).
- The "unknown trace parent" log in obs-ingest seems to come from the span-assembler stage where we expect a parent ID to stitch; when parent missing we currently drop by default (we used to create a synthetic root, but a change in PR #678 altered behavior).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) recent SDK rollout (service.version 1.2.+) introduced a label encoding change causing otel-collector -> obs-ingest unmarshal to fail on some messages, leading to partial drops and consumer retries -> lag -> backpressure -> more drops. (High confidence)
2) Some frontend paths drop traceparent on redirects (edge CDN rewrite) causing orphan spans that obs-ingest currently drops instead of creating a synthetic root. (Moderate)
3) Kafka broker rebalancing occasionally yields out-of-order offsets causing the consumer to skip a range; our consumer doesn't handle the specific timestamp-based reordering well. (Low->Medium)

Quick experiments attempted and outcomes:
- Rolled back obs-ingest config to accept unknown resource labels (tolerate unknown fields) -> small improvement but did not eliminate gaps.
- Replayed samples with and without traceparent -> reproducible orphan behavior confirmed.
- Forced a consumer restart after compaction -> temporarily cleared lag but pattern reappeared with traffic.

Immediate action items (what I did / to do):
- [done] Add DEBUG logs around span-assembler to capture incoming span headers and raw resource labels for 1% of traffic (feature flag: debug.span_assembler=true).
- [done] Attach PR link for revert candidate (review PR #678 for the behavior change).
- [todo] Add temporary synthetic-root fallback when parent absent for 24h window to see effect on trace-coverage metric. Roll out behind flag. (owner: Evan)
- [todo] Add a consumer-side metric for "messages failed unmarshal due to labels" and alert when > 0.1% of traffic. (owner: Priya)
- [todo] Re-run replay tests with 5k messages preserving headers and analyze percentage accepted vs dropped.
- [todo] Ask CDN team if a recent change around redirects/edge rewrites removed traceparent on 302. Slack: <#C67890> ping.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is PR #678 the root cause or just a contributor? I need diff of codec change and tests that justified dropping synthetic-root behaviour.
- Are the malformed resource labels coming from a single service rollout or multiple services? Need a sampling of incoming service.name/service.version combos.
- Is the kafka broker config using message.timestamp ordering that can be tuned? Check broker logs for partition leader changes at spike times.

Notes to self (debug checklist next time):
- When spike alert fires: 1) snapshot kafka consumer offsets & lag; 2) capture obs-ingest pod logs with --previous; 3) enable debug.span_assembler for 1 minute; 4) dump otel-collector metrics.
- Keep replay tool handy: tools/replayer.py and sample-requests.json in repo root.

References + breadcrumbs for follow-up:
- OBS-412 (epic) — root ticket with linked service rollout notes.
- PR #678 (obs-pipeline) — changed span assembly/synthetic root behaviour.
- Confluence obs-pipeline design page (link above).
- Slack thread: #observability (C67890) — thread around 2025-10-16 with CDN team.

Final quick thought:
I think the fastest mitigation to reduce user pain: enable synthetic-root fallback behind an org-level feature flag and monitor. If coverage recovers, we revert the change in PR #678 later and make the encoding tolerant. Rolling back a behavioral change (even temporarily) will buy time to do a cleaner fix for the label encoding.

-- Aisha
